name: GoogleOther
job_en: Generic crawl for various Google product teams
follows_en: Yes. Google says common crawlers always obey robots.txt rules when crawling automatically.

ips.note: Google says the common crawlers generally crawl from the ranges in common-crawlers.json, and that the reverse DNS name matches crawl-***-***-***-***.googlebot.com or geo-crawl-***-***-***-***.geo.googlebot.com.

vendor_quote: GoogleOther is the generic crawler that may be used by various product teams for fetching publicly accessible content from sites. For example, it may be used for one-off crawls for internal research and development.

vendor_quote_source.title: Google Search Central: Google's common crawlers

what_en: GoogleOther is Google's generic crawler, used by various Google product teams to fetch publicly accessible content, for example in one-off crawls for internal research and development. Google lists it among its common crawlers, next to Googlebot, and also documents GoogleOther-Image and GoogleOther-Video as versions optimized for image and video URLs. The Google page does not say it is used for AI training.
block_en: Google says crawling preferences addressed to the GoogleOther user agent do not affect any specific product. Google documents GoogleOther-Image and GoogleOther-Video as separate robots.txt tokens, so a rule for GoogleOther is not stated to cover them, and the Googlebot token is a separate token again.
compare_en: Googlebot crawls for Google Search and related products, while GoogleOther is a generic crawler whose robots.txt rules do not affect any specific Google product.

sources.title: Google Search Central: Google's common crawlers
Google Search Central: Overview of Google crawlers and fetchers

notes: Google page does not say GoogleOther is AI-related; it says generic/R&D. Common-crawlers page also lives at developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers (same content). Chrome/W.X.Y.Z is Google's version placeholder. Page last updated 2026-10-15 per Google.
answer_en: GoogleOther is Google's generic crawler. Various Google product teams use it to fetch publicly accessible content, for example in one-off crawls for internal research and development. Google says rules addressed to GoogleOther do not affect any specific product. GoogleOther-Image and GoogleOther-Video are documented as separate tokens.
